title: The Big Laugh

format_analysis.format: An AI 3D talking-character duet: a Pixar-style panty liner vs a talking pair of plain black underwear, staged as an A-vs-B pair from frame 0. It opens in media res on a friend's off-screen laugh. Every line is fast character comedy, cut with real-product inserts and location hops, and it ends on a brand end card with a quiz CTA.
format_analysis.how_it_should_look: LOOK: Pixar-quality 3D characters composited into a photoreal set, at the realism level of Everdries 1700150534480418 but lovable instead of grotesque. SET (change from the script, Nikita to OK): a golden-hour bistro instead of candle-lit. A big window frame-left with low sun, warm pendant-bulb bokeh, Warm Cream linen, a blush/tan clutch with a gold clasp, a Claret napkin as the one accent, sparkling water with lemon, and one small lit tealight as the 'evening' nod (not the key light). Frame 0 sits at bright mid-high exposure. The black underwear always gets a rim light and visible fabric texture, never crushed blacks. CAMERA: a smooth tripod/dolly feel with gentle in-camera push-ins plus edit punch-ins (110-125%, generated at the highest resolution so they stay sharp). No handheld on character shots. The real-product inserts are phone-real, naturally lit and graded to the same warmth. ANGLE LIBRARY (never the same angle on two consecutive lines): tabletop two-shot (F1), low-angle brace (F2), MCU underwear (F3), OTS from behind the underwear (F4), low-angle hero underwear (F5), high-angle deflated liner (F8), CU gag (F9), inside-the-clutch POV looking up (F10), reverse two-shot backlit (F12), ECU reaction (F17), high angle into the clutch (F18). LOCATIONS: bistro table -> inside the clutch -> restaurant restroom -> laundry -> drying rack -> bedroom dresser -> back to the table. CAPTIONS: Hanken Grotesk ExtraBold, Plum Ink on Warm Cream boxes mid-frame (~50-55%). The hook is a Claret pill with cream text. Fraunces only on the end-card wordmark and lines. SOUND: restaurant ambience, a licensed pizzicato/ukulele comedic underscore ducked under dialogue, and an SFX on every cut in the first 10s. Two distinct character voices plus one off-screen friend voice.
format_analysis.runtime_main: 31.2s. Every scripted line is kept. The script's ~25s beat timings can't hold its 82 spoken words; a trim path to ~25s is in pacing_check.vo_fit_issues for Nikita to OK.
format_analysis.build_profile: HOOK 0-2.6s: no human on screen. The off-screen friend's laugh and line come from stock group-laugh SFX plus an ElevenLabs LP_FRIEND voice (a 30s woman, mid-laugh, using v3 [laughing] tags). The liner lip-syncs from 1.4s. SETUP/REVEAL/BODY 2.6-17.9s: on-camera 3D characters, one speaker per clip, with the non-speaker silent and mouth closed. Voices are ElevenLabs Voice Design voices shared across V2-a/b/c. LP_LINER is higher, fussy and fast, with a comedic squeak on stressed words. LP_UNDIES is a warm, dry, unhurried mid-30s deadpan. Accent: Australian, to match the AUD launch market (Nikita to OK). Real-product inserts run 8.5-10.7s and 17.9-21.7s with the underwear voice as off-screen VO, so no lip-sync is needed. The AI woman at 21.7-23.8s is silent and getting dressed only. CTA/END 24.5-31.2s: the liner's sulk line on-face, then the underwear's CTA lip-synced on the end card. Record all VO first (one continuous read per character) and cut the animatic to it before generating video.

reference_ads.what_we_take: UltraDries' Pixar winner (video #4, 104d). The talking pad moves to a NEW room on line changes (living room -> bathroom vanity -> bedroom -> kitchen table -> bedside) and changes size and angle every cut, with bright, warm, lamp-lit interiors. We copy the location hop on 'sulk' (inside-clutch POV) and on 'trash' (restroom bin), plus an angle change on every line. We skip its word-by-word yellow captions and the human reactor.

Everdries talking objects (208d). Each object lives in its own photoreal, bright set (marble counter, tub edge, washer), with one pill caption per phrase. Its slim white 'flimsy panty liner' is our liner's silhouette reference. We fix its weakness: ~7s single-angle speaker holds (ours are 2.8s max) and the grotesque villain faces (ours stay lovable and stain-free).

UltraDries pad-vs-underwear duet. The black underwear stands UPRIGHT with its face on the front panel, both characters are in a two-shot on frame 0, reframes come every ~2-3s, then it cuts to a human/demo insert. We take the upright-underwear staging, the face placement (we move it higher: upper front, just under the waistband) and the insert break. We drop its stained, yellowed pad, its static single bed set, the pour demo and all claims.
Everdries POV hook (video #14, 275d). An emoji pops in at ~1s as a motion event inside a held hook shot, with the text held ~3s. We copy it as the laughing-emoji pop at 0.7s inside our 2.6s hook.

recommended.on_screen_timing: 0.0s-2.6s: fully on at frame 0 with no animate-in, held for the whole hook shot, out on the cut to F2. A laughing-emoji sticker pops beside it at 0.7s. Labels 'panty liner' / 'underwear' pop at 0.2s.
recommended.style: Claret #A33154 pill, cream #F5EDE6 Hanken Grotesk ExtraBold, 2 lines ('Stop!' / 'I'll pee myself!'). Cap height ~6% of frame, centred at ~22-30% height inside the 4:5 crop. Typographic quote marks so it reads as a HEARD line. One soft scale-breath (100->103%) at the laugh peak (~0.5s).
recommended.why: It's the best fit for THIS visual hook, so keep the locked line. (1) The text IS the in-media-res moment (Miro #38): it's the line being shouted as the liner bursts out, so text, audio and picture say one thing. (2) It names 'pee' at 0.0s. (3) It's first person, so it passes Meta's personal-attributes rule (no 'you leak'). (4) At 4 words it reads in under 0.5s. (5) It's the live H1, so the landing scent is word for word. Proven base: the trigger-moment angle A7 (Everdries 'laugh' ~110 live) and the 30-45 clinic hook '...the leaking when you laugh, sneeze, lift a box...' (103d). Its one weakness: a muted viewer can read it as the LINER talking. The quote marks, the emoji, the laugh-jolt and the 'panty liner' label fix that.

alternates.why: The shortest, cleanest moment line: 4 words, pee at 0.0s, no speaker ambiguity, bare third-person-neutral moment (Meta-safe). The best hook-isolation test against the locked line, because it changes only the first read and keeps the picture.
alternates.proven_anchor: Trigger-moment hooks: Everdries 'laugh' wording (~110 live) and the clinic line '…the leaking when you laugh, sneeze, lift a box, or jump on the trampoline with your kids.' (103d).

alternates.text: Big laugh, little pee. / Panty liner or underwear?
alternates.why: Makes the A-vs-B comparison explicit in the text, re-attaching the unproven talking-object format to the best-proven engine. It opens a loop the ad answers. Two lines; line 1 reads in 0.5s.
alternates.proven_anchor: 'Old versus new Everdries, what's the difference?' (Carol, video #10) on the A-vs-B format F1, which has 8 top-5% hits (Carol 1629603918494594, 275d, #1 on its page).

alternates.text: It's 2026. Still packing a panty liner?
alternates.why: The contrarian 'still?' frame is the longest-running problem-object hook in the set, and it fits the clutch gag. No 'you' and no condition, so it's Meta-safe, and it's not a pads-fail claim (CJ-safe). Caveat: there's no 'pee' in the text, so on sound-off it breaks the campaign's pee-in-first-3s rule unless F2's caption carries it. Use it only as a third test cell.
alternates.proven_anchor: 'It's 2025! Why are you still using pads?' (Everdries 1206351388295667, 275d, 6 dupes, video #14).

text_hook.note: The recommended text is the locked script line. The only differences are styling: typographic quote marks, the laughing-emoji pop at 0.7s, and the label 'liner' -> 'panty liner' (word rule). Nikita chiefs. If he wants a hook-isolation cell, alternate 1 swaps only the pill text and nothing else.

visual_hook_build.miro: #38 In Media Res Start + #117 3D Talking Character
visual_hook_build.frame_1: A tight 3/4 tabletop shot on a golden-hour bistro table. An open blush clutch, with the white panty-liner character already 60% out of it mid-burst: arched back, tab-hands up, eyes huge, mouth an 'O'. A tissue and a gold lipstick are airborne above the bag and the flap is mid-swing. The plain black underwear character stands upright right beside the clutch, deadpan, its face on the upper front panel under the waistband and its full silhouette readable. Water ripples in a sparkling-water glass. The frame is mid-jolt (edit shake). The Claret pill “Stop! I'll pee myself!” is already on at ~22-30% height and the AI label at ~60%. Bright and window-lit with warm bokeh; nothing dark.
build_steps: 1. SHARED CHARACTER ANCHOR: LINER (LP_LINER, same in V2-a/b/c). A slim, softly rounded, wingless-silhouette panty liner, ~2-3mm thin, with a quilted micro-dimple top sheet. Pure clean white with a pale-mint unbranded peel strip on the back. Big glossy round eyes in the top third, small expressive brows, a mouth at mid-body, and two small soft tab-hands from the sides (cartoon arms, not pad wings, so it never reads as a thick winged pad). It moves by hopping and bending at the middle. It's fussy, eager and lovable. NEVER: stains, yellowing, backlit core show-through, brand marks, or a villain/gross-out face. Nano Banana Pro turnaround sheet (front, 3/4, side, back) plus 6 expressions (eager, panicked 'O', incredulous, deflated, sulky, sheepish), registered as a Higgsfield reference element / Kling element.

2. SHARED CHARACTER ANCHOR: UNDERWEAR (LP_UNDIES, same in V2-a/b/c). Built ONLY from the 5 CJ sample photos (SKU CJNSNYNK00343: flat front, flat back, side, stretched, under leggings). Rise, waistband width, leg line and sheen are copied from the photos, not from text. Plain black, no lace, no logo, no gusset or seams that aren't on the sample, wider at the back. FACE: two calm oval eyes with soft white sclera and a Rose Taupe lid line (so they read on black), and a small dry mouth. The eyes sit one finger-width below the waistband seam, and the mouth ends ABOVE the line where the leg openings start to curve in. Nothing below that line: the gusset zone stays blank and is never the face. Brows are subtle fabric creases; the one-brow lift is its signature. It stands upright on its leg openings like the 1691171645641479 underwear. It moves by waistband shrugs and folding nods, and has no arms. It's warm, dry, deadpan and unbothered. Turnaround (front, 3/4, back) plus 4 expressions (deadpan, brow-lift, dry half-smile, smug nod), registered as a reference element.

3. SET PLATE (V2-b anchor): Nano Banana Pro, 9:16, 2k, no characters. Golden-hour bistro window table: Warm Cream linen, blush/tan leather clutch with a gold clasp (NOT black: a black clutch merges with the black underwear's silhouette), Claret napkin, tall sparkling water with lemon, a side plate with a fork, one small lit tealight, window frame-left with low sun, pendant-bulb bokeh behind, no wine anywhere, no people, no logos. Compose the clutch and the underwear's spot at ~35-55% height, so the pill (22-30%) sits above them and the labels (36-42%) sit between.

4. START FRAME: on the approved plate, generate with both reference elements. The liner is at the burst apex-minus, 60% out of the bag, arched back, tab-hands splayed with a subtle motion smear, mouth 'O'. The tissue and unbranded gold lipstick are airborne 3-5cm above the bag, the flap swinging (edge blur), the water tilted with a ripple ring, the fork mid-bounce. The underwear stands upright beside the clutch, deadpan, eyes half-lidded, mouth closed. Check at phone size with the pill, labels and AI line mocked on top.

5. ANIMATE FROM MID-MOTION: Veo 3.1 start-frame, 8s, with a prompt that says everything is ALREADY moving. The liner continues up and out of the bag, flips once and lands upright on the clutch rim with a wobble. The lipstick and tissue fall back in, the flap settles and the ripple decays. The underwear stays perfectly still; only its eyes slide toward the liner and one brow lifts. Slow 4% push-in, no new objects, no people, native audio muted. If Veo eases in from rest, use Kling 2.x/3.0 start+end frame (end frame = liner braced on the rim) to force the trajectory.
6. TRIM FOR A MOVING FRAME 0: start the edit 4-8 frames into the clip, so the published frame 0 is already in motion (the models ease in from the still).

7. EDIT-SIDE HOOK EVENTS (CapCut, zero gen cost): a 0.00-0.25s table jolt (8px vertical shake, 2 cycles, 1 deg rotate) synced to a palm-thump in the laugh; the pill on at frame 0; labels pop at 0.2s; the laughing-emoji pop at 0.7s; a slight pill scale-breath at 0.5s.

8. OFF-SCREEN LAUGH AUDIO: a licensed 3-4-woman restaurant laugh (Meta Sound Collection / Epidemic / Artlist), pre-rolled 0.3s so frame 0 lands mid-laugh. On top, the ElevenLabs LP_FRIEND voice: “Stop — stop! I'll pee myself!” with [laughing] tags, at 0.2-1.4s, panned slightly off-centre as if across the table. It's a third voice, distinct from both characters. No human appears on screen.
9. LINER LIP-SYNC 1.4-2.6s: ElevenLabs LP_LINER 'That's a big laugh —', lip-synced (Path B) onto the liner only. The underwear's mouth stays closed (one speaker per clip).

10. VOICE PATH, PER CLIP: lock it after the F3 A/B test. Default to Path A (Veo 3.1 native acting + ElevenLabs Voice Changer into the saved voice) for short, physical lines: F2, F4, F8, F9, F11, F12, F17. Use Path B (ElevenLabs first + Hedra Character-3 / Kling lip-sync) where the timing is locked to the cut or the light is tricky: F1, F5, F10, F18, S19. Never single-track lip-sync two faces.
visual_hook_build.lane_and_tool: AI start frame + motion: Nano Banana Pro on Higgsfield (9:16, 2k, both reference elements) for the start frame, then Veo 3.1 start-frame (or Kling 2.x/3.0 start+end frame for the burst trajectory). Audio from licensed stock laugh SFX + ElevenLabs (LP_FRIEND, LP_LINER). Jolt, pill, labels and emoji in CapCut (editor). All tools are recommendations until Nikita confirms the generator.
visual_hook_build.fallback: If the burst won't animate cleanly in 2 rerolls: use a start frame with the liner already standing on the clutch rim mid-wobble (tab-hands windmilling), a Kling start+end frame for a 0.5s hop, and let the edit carry the in-media-res (pre-rolled laugh, 0.0s table jolt, the airborne lipstick composited from the still). If the underwear can't be built because there are no CJ photos, V2-b doesn't ship. Meanwhile, lock the liner, the set, the VO and a placeholder animatic.
failure_modes_to_reject: Frame 0 static or easing in from rest (the liner sitting still in the bag): the in-media-res is lost.
A dark or candle-dim frame 0 (average luminance low), or the black underwear crushed to a featureless blob or merging with a dark clutch.
The underwear's face low on the garment, near or on the gusset/crotch, or features below the leg-opening curve line.
The underwear morphing into a boyshort, thong or lace, or gaining a logo, label text, visible seams/gusset not on the sample, or the wrong sheen or waistband width vs the photos.
The liner reading as a thick winged pad, or showing any stain, yellowing, backlit core or brand mark, or a grotesque/villain face.
Two mouths moving in one clip, or the underwear lip-flapping while the liner talks; lip-sync drift or mushy mouth shapes (regenerate, don't fix in the edit).
Any human, hand, arm or face entering the hook or any character shot.
Wine glasses, bottles or any alcohol anywhere in frame, including the bokeh.
Real or lookalike logos on the clutch hardware, the bin, the washer or the perfume.
Gibberish text or signage generated in frame (paint it out or reroll; all text is added in CapCut).
The liner inside the bin, or shown loose/unwrapped on a floor (reads as used).
Extra limbs or fused tab-hands, or the liner changing size or shape between cuts (reference-element drift).
Veo native music or extra voices bleeding into the track (mute native audio except Path A dialogue).
Any water, liquid, pour or 'dry result' visual (CJ column).

shots.angle_or_room: Tabletop two-shot, 3/4 front, camera ~30 deg above the table, 50mm look, f/2 bokeh. Golden-hour bistro window table (replaces 'candle-lit', Nikita to OK).
shots.what_we_see: Frame 0 is mid-chaos. A blush/tan leather clutch with a gold clasp lies open on a Warm Cream linen tablecloth, its flap flung back and still swinging. The clean white panty-liner character is ALREADY 60% out of the bag, arched back mid-burst: tab-hands flung up, eyes huge, mouth an 'O'. A folded tissue and an unbranded gold lipstick hang in the air above the bag. The plain black underwear character stands upright on the table right beside the clutch, with its waistband at clutch-top height so the whole silhouette reads as underwear. It's deadpan, eyes half-lidded, face on the upper front panel just under the waistband. Low sun from frame-left rims the underwear's waistband and backlights the liner's edges. Behind: warm pendant-bulb bokeh and a window. A tall sparkling water with lemon and a Claret napkin (the one accent) sit frame-right. No person, no hands, no wine.
shots.motion_inside_shot: Physics is already moving at frame 0 (the edit starts 4-8 frames into the gen). 0.00-0.25s: table micro-jolt (edit shake 8px/1 deg, synced to a palm-on-table thump in the laugh), a ripple ring in the water, a fork bounces on the side plate. 0.2s: labels pop. 0.4-0.9s: the liner springs fully out, flips once and lands upright on the clutch rim with a wobble; tissue and lipstick drop back in. 0.7s: a laughing-emoji sticker pops beside the pill. 1.2s: the underwear's eyes slide to the liner and one brow lifts (signature deadpan). 1.4s: the liner turns to the lens and starts talking. Slow 4% push-in throughout.
shots.on_screen_text: HOOK: a Claret pill with cream Hanken Grotesk ExtraBold, 2 lines, centred at ~22-30% height. It is on at frame 0 with no animate-in: “Stop! I'll pee myself!”, with a laughing-emoji pop at 0.7s. Labels at 0.2s (small cream text on Plum Ink 85% pills, ~36-42% height): 'panty liner' above the liner, 'underwear' beside the underwear. Persistent AI label (tiny, cream 80% on a Plum Ink 50% box, ~60% height): 'AI-generated. Not real customers.'
shots.vo_or_dialogue: OFF-SCREEN FRIEND (audio only, already mid-laugh at frame 0, 0.2-1.4s): “Stop — stop! I'll pee myself!”  LINER (1.4-2.6s, fast, eager): “That's a big laugh —”
shots.sfx: Restaurant ambience. A 3-4-woman laugh burst pre-rolled 0.3s so frame 0 is mid-laugh. Table thump at 0.0s, glass shimmer, fork rattle, cartoon spring 'boing' on the liner's flip. A pizzicato/ukulele underscore enters at 1.0s, ducked under dialogue.
shots.cut_reason: Cuts on the em-dash ('big laugh —') into the brace, so the line's turn is the action beat. One 2.6s hook shot with 5 motion events inside and no cut before 2.6s (pacing law 1; creative-plan rule: max 1 cut in the first 1.2s).
shots.tool_rec: Nano Banana Pro start frame (Higgsfield, 9:16, 2k, both character reference elements on the bistro plate). Animate with Veo 3.1 start-frame, 8s, native audio muted. If Veo eases in from rest, use Kling 2.x/3.0 start+end frame instead (end frame = liner braced on the rim). Use 2.6s. Voice: Path B, ElevenLabs liner line first, then lip-sync the liner only (1.4-2.6s); the underwear's mouth stays closed. Jolt, pill, labels and emoji in CapCut.

pacing_check.broll_or_insert_share: 40% inserts + location hops (12.4s), including 26% real product or product-on-body (8.1s). Two-shots are only 11% (3.5s); the end card is 15%. Single-character + insert coverage (everything that isn't a two-shot or the card) = 74%.
vo_fit_issues: WHOLE SCRIPT: 82 spoken words. At the brief's 2.4 words/s that's ~34s. At a brisk cartoon pace (liner ~3.2 w/s, underwear ~2.6 w/s) plus 0.15s J-cuts it's 31.2s. The script's 25.0s beat timings can't hold the lines, so this board keeps every line and runs 31.2s.
Script beat 2 (1.4-3.6s, 2.2s) holds 13 spoken words (~4.5s even at a fast pace). On this board it spans 1.4-5.9s.
Script beat 4 (7.6-13.2s, 5.6s) holds 25 spoken words (~8-9s). On this board it spans 10.7-19.8s.
Script beat 6 end card (20.2-25.0s, 4.8s) holds 18 words (~6.7s). The board splits it into the liner's sulk shot F18 (2.1s) + the end card S19 (4.6s), so the card stays under 5s.
Tightest single line: the F1 liner's 'That's a big laugh —' is 4 words in 1.2s (3.3 w/s). That's OK for a fast fussy voice; if the read runs long, apply T5.

TRIM PATH TO ~25s (Nikita OK needed; no line has been changed without it). T1: drop the repeated 'She could just wear underwear.' so S15 plays under 'Pull them on.' (-0.9s). T2: drop 'Okay, fine.' + 'And you?' by cutting F8 + F12 and moving the pills onto F9 (-1.7s). T3: shorten the end-card CTA to 'Take the quiz, find your match.' and fold the liner's sulk line onto the card (F18+S19 6.7s -> 4.6s, -2.1s). T4: 'Underwear? For the laugh?!' becomes a 0.6s silent 'huh?!' reaction, per the script's own 20s TRIM note (-0.7s). T5: drop 'That's a big laugh —' (-0.4s). Total about -5.8s, landing at ~25.4s.
pacing_check.notes: How this beats the refs: the #4 Pixar winner (1400650075258672) averages 3.6s with 2 cuts in 3-10s. This board averages 1.64s with 5 hard cuts plus 2 punch-ins in 3-10s (7 visual changes, near the 8 of the #6 winner), 5 location hops plus the return to the table, and no angle repeated on consecutive lines. Everdries 1700150534480418's ~7s single-speaker holds become a 2.8s max character hold, and 1691171645641479's static bed two-shot shrinks to 11% of runtime. The hook is one continuous 2.6s shot with 5 motion events (jolt, label pop, emoji pop, liner flip-and-land, underwear brow-lift) and an SFX on every cut in the first 10s. Deliberate exception: 10.7-12.7s runs 0.8s and 1.2s staccato shots locked to the liner's one-word confessions (law 3 asks for 2-3s shots after 10s); from 14.2s the rhythm returns to ~2-3s, except the word-locked 'Wash./Hang.' pair. LONG CUT (~35s retargeting): split the foil and care exchange back out and add a 2nd real-sample insert (a different getting-ready move) before the end card, about +4s on this board.
